correctness.rationale: The simplex-linear W and explicit phi,g satisfy every C1–C3 hypothesis; g iterates are summable. Row identities P_n=P+4^{-n}(E-P) prove summable perturbation and positive tail bounds for all reversed products. Convex-hull trapping gives nonconvergence to P; Dobrushin submultiplicativity and column extrema prove rank-one limits and superexponential weak mixing. Exact-rational 152 finite two-state tests corroborate, not replace, the universal analytical argument.

value.rationale: A central 2024 uniform-ergodicity theorem, used in later entangled Markov-chain arguments, fails under all published assumptions. The counterexample is nondegenerate in every dimension and for all strictly interior initial row collections, despite geometric orbit convergence and superexponential weak mixing. It exhibits precise persistent rightmost-factor memory and diagnoses the missing two-sided projection commutation by comparison with the cited original perturbation theorem.
